strengths: Seat-7 is genuinely fixed: the repPeak high-water mark (h.repPeak>=3.5) correctly rewards a line that built a strong reputation even if it has softened since, and the forward signal in houseCharacter() and the readout panel explicitly names what is needed — no longer a dead branch.
Motto diversity is real across sampled play: 5 dynasties produced 4 distinct mottos (scholarly, artistic x2, industrious, generous) with no majority, confirming the 1.0 bump equalization worked.

The bequest lever is the single cleanest cross-generation agency point in the genre: one late-life choice (mind / means / heart / freedom) tangibly shifts the heir's starting conditions in documented, diegetically honest ways, and the heir screen names it explicitly.

The reckoning (x_reckoning) is well-designed competing-goods pressure: seat-3+ gate, once-per-life, and the 'fell' branch directly costs a seat — narrated in the moment via logLine so the player feels the dynasty fall rather than inferring it later.
Seat movement is narrated in the moment (the logLine at death that says 'The family climbed / slipped this generation') rather than left for the heir screen, which closes the feedback loop elegantly.

The cb_the_cost callback is the strongest systems-design choice in the whole card set: it reads back which competing-goods memory is active and individualises the elder reckoning, making past choices feel genuinely consequential decades later.

Trait-gated cards (bookish, guarded, restless) and seat-gated cards (s_great_burden, s_from_nothing, s_patronage) create meaningfully different play-contexts for different dynasties — the content layer gates real opportunities, not flavour.
Heirloom propagation is mechanically sound: the inherited:{true} guard prevents stale heirlooms from silently re-scoring reputation every generation, which was the original collapse vector.

improvements.what: Add 'industrious' as a direct option in a_make_name alongside learned/hard-to-cross/open-handed, with a do() that sets p.flags.legacy='built' or remember('self_made'). Currently industrious is only reachable indirectly via scattered self_made/built_the_name/driven memories, making it the least steerable of the nine reputation tags despite being bump-equalized.
improvements.why: A player who wants to build an industrious house has no reliable intentional lever — they depend on incidentally picking fork-career, m_invest_name, or m_rival choices. Scholarly, generous, and ruthless all have direct steering paths; industrious does not.

improvements.what: Surface the repPeak mechanic one seat earlier: when seat>=5 (not only seat>=6), the houseCharacter() readout or the 'how things stand' direction hint should mention that the reputation high-water mark — not only the current value — is what the histories gate on. Something like 'even a reputation that has softened counts toward it, if it was once strong enough.'
improvements.why: The seat-7 gate requires repPeak>=3.5, which players cannot observe directly. A seat-5 family with strong historic reputation has already built the credential but gets no signal that it is accumulating credit toward the pinnacle. The forward signal only appears at seat-6, one step too late for meaningful planning.

improvements.what: Add a second reckoning variant — or lower the cool from 26 to ~18 — so a long-lived dynasty (6+ generations, 400+ years of game-time) faces at least two reckonings. Currently a 7-generation house can statistically go the entire run with a single reckoning, reducing the fall-pressure that makes seat-holding feel earned.
improvements.why: The reckoning is the primary downward-pressure mechanic. A cool of 26 years per life means a 90-year life only risks one instance; at 26-year cooldown across multiple lives, a strong house can simply age past the threat. Two reckonings would make the 'held' branch feel more like a repeated test of dynastic character.

verdict: A genuinely excellent generational system: the seat-7 fix is real and correctly gated, motto diversity is verified across sampled play, the bequest-reckoning-callback triad gives players meaningful levers across the generation boundary, and the narrative feedback is timed to the causal moment — the only remaining gap is that industrious is the one reputation without a direct steering card, which is a smaller omission than any of the previous rounds' blockers.
